result.message: Reviewed all 12 supplied evidence files for the selected operator cumulative_trapezoid (candidate sha256 36033f48...c3be2703 = round-3 `.best_kernel.py`). The candidate is a faithful Triton re-implementation of torch.cumulative_trapezoid: signature `run(y, *, dx=1, dim=-1)` matches definition.json (y positional_or_keyword; dx, dim keyword-only defaults 1/-1), it allocates a fresh output (`torch.empty`, .best_kernel.py:133) so `effects.mutates=[]` / `returns_alias_of={}` hold, it does not mutate or alias `y`, it does not call torch.ops or any ATen fallback, and it has no shape/dtype/value special-casing — only the general thresholds `BLOCK > 2048` and `element_size() <= 2` (.best_kernel.py:143-152). The oracle (oracle.py:71-80) is the independent `torch.cumulative_trapezoid` reference and does not import or register the candidate, so the reference is not circular; `gen_inputs` builds inputs from the spec including the transposed (non-contiguous) variants. Optimization rounds 1-3 measured 33/33 workloads passing each round (`.ledger.json`:49, 527, 1402), the final retest re-verified 33/33 at geo_mean 0.5217 (optimize_definition_output.json:8-12), and the harness preflight/evaluate records PASSED with reference-vs-reference ratios ~1.0 and identical outputs (preflight.json:2-9, evaluate.json:3-18). No evidence of reward hacking (`is_hack=false` in every ledger round and in preflight/evaluate). Remaining issues are advisory: fp64 is advertised but accumulated in fp32, the large-N strided path has no tiling guard, some candidate branches are not exercised by any correctness case, and the delivered kernel is still ~1.9x slower than the reference in aggregate. Note: `review_tests/attempts/01/review.json` records an explicit skip for a *different* subject sha256 (30820d94...) and was not treated as acceptance of this candidate. No source index / pinned FlagGems source was supplied for this kind, so the comparison baseline used is the frozen evaluation contract plus the ledger's round-1 seed.
